title: Level design basics: Guiding players without telling them
summary: Level design basics for beginners: How light, color, landmarks, leading lines, and breadcrumbs guide players through a game, and how to test your own levels.
body_markdown:
## What level design does


A big part of level design is helping players with two things: knowing where they are, and finding a route to where they want to go. Level design is also how a game introduces new abilities, paces them out, and[teaches players how to use them](https://unity.com/blog/find-your-core-game-loop) .


Good level design[starts with purpose](https://unity.com/blog/one-page-game-design-document) . The shape of a space should come from what’s meant to happen there. A combat area in a shooter, for example, needs objects to hide behind, while an area built for a chase needs room to run.


One important mindset: You’re not trying to trick players into going where you want. Players often wander off the main route on purpose, to explore side areas or play at their own pace, and that’s a valid way to play. A more useful way to think about it is that you’re giving players the information and tools they need to use your level however they choose.
